proof_summary: For the gcd numerator, the added integers \(np+1,\ldots,np+k\) contain no multiple of \(p\), so every newly introduced gcd has zero \(p\)-adic valuation. For the factorial denominator, Legendre’s formula rewrites its valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}\sum_{m\le \lfloor N/p^i\rfloor}m\lfloor\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor/m\rfloor\), which is unchanged because \(\lfloor(np+k)/p^i\rfloor=\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\) for \(k<p\); comparison with the numerator’s corresponding terms \(\lfloor N/p^i\rfloor^2\) also proves the denominator divides the numerator, allowing subtraction of valuations.
